guide.headline: Cowboys pass game vs Houston pressure decides this one
guide.hook: Dallas has two different ways to break Houston through the air, and Will Anderson Jr. is the one defender who can wreck the plan by himself.

items.title: Cowboys own third-and-long
items.what: The Cowboys are No. 2 of 32 on passing downs at 55 percent success, and the defense ranks No. 15 at 36 percent, a 42 percentile point gap. That is a clear edge for Dallas. Two conversions in the first half break the defense's plan.
items.when: Third-and-long situations, especially in the first half.
items.who: Cowboys on passing downs vs Texans pressure

items.title: Will Anderson Jr. chases four sacks
items.what: Anderson has 10 tackles, 6 TFL, 4 sacks and 6 QB hits this season, top 1 percent of NFL edge rushers, while playing 82 percent of defensive snaps as the top left end. Watch his get-off at the snap and whether he bends the arc or also sets the edge against the run.
items.when: Early downs and obvious passing downs when he lines up wide.

items.title: Dallas tests the deep shell
items.what: The Cowboys rank No. 18 of 32 in pass explosiveness at 1.30, but the defense they face is dead last, No. 32, at limiting explosive passes at 1.67, a 45 percentile point gap. Watch the first deep shot: if it connects, the coverage has to change shells and the run game opens up underneath.
items.when: First or second drive, first deep shot attempt.
items.who: Cowboys deep passing vs Texans secondary

guide.cardLine: Watch whether the Cowboys convert third-and-long and hit an early deep shot, while Will Anderson Jr. tries to blow it up himself.
